appraisal_events.evidence: Comme Mme Verdurin, malgré de petites exagérations un peu risibles, a un amour sincère de la peinture, de la musique ! Quelle passion pour les oeuvres, quel désir de faire plaisir aux artistes !
appraisal_events.explanation: In Swann's free indirect self-persuasion, he credits Mme Verdurin with a sincere love of art and generosity toward artists, though the concession about 'laughable exaggerations' and the surrounding rhetorical excess signal the narrator's ironic distance from Swann's own reverie.

appraisal_events.evidence: je me plais parfaitement bien avec Cottard, quoiqu'il fasse des calembours ineptes
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann admits enjoying Cottard's company but dismisses his wordplay as inept, a faint, backhanded acknowledgment embedded in Swann's list of self-justifications for the milieu.

appraisal_events.evidence: si sa prétention est déplaisante quand il cherche à étonner, en revanche c'est une des plus belles intelligences que j'aie connues
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann faults the painter's pretension but counters it with strong praise, calling him one of the finest minds he has known, within the same self-persuading catalogue of the salon's merits.

status_effects.explanation: Locally credited with genuine artistic passion and generosity, though the praise arrives filtered through Swann's self-serving rationalization of the Verdurin milieu.
Despite a jab at his pretension, Swann elevates him as one of the finest minds he has known.

ambiguities: The entire closing paragraph is Swann's interior monologue talking himself into loving the Verdurin milieu; whether the narrator intends genuine endorsement of these three praised figures or is exposing Swann's self-delusion (a reading well supported by the broader arc of 'Un amour de Swann') cannot be settled from this passage alone, so stances are marked ironized and deltas kept conservative.
